# QA Story 842: Work each job from a room-by-room checklist with photo proof

Run a full QA session for this story. Two phases: write a testing brief,
then execute it. The playbook below has the detailed procedure.

**App URL:** Run `mix run -e 'IO.puts(CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url())'`.

## Story description

As a cleaner, I want each job to present a room-by-room checklist defining exactly what's in scope, with the ability to check off tasks and attach before/after photos, so that scope is never ambiguous and I'm protected from "missed spot" blame for tasks that weren't agreed to. (Research: scope ambiguity is the top cleaner frustration; photo checklists proven by STR tools — pain-points §2.1, §3.3)

## Acceptance criteria

- Checklist opens grouped by room
- Out-of-scope task is not on the checklist
- Checking tasks advances progress
- Before and after photos attach to a task
- Job completes when all required items are done
- Completion blocked with a required task unchecked
- Photo taken offline uploads when signal returns

# Qa Story Brief

Per-story QA testing brief. Written by the QA planner after reading the story's prompt file and the QA plan. Gives the tester exact instructions — tool, auth, seeds, what to test.

## Required Sections

### Tool

Format:
- Use H2 heading
- Single line: tool name (web, curl, or script path)

Content:
- Which tool to use for this story's testing
- `web` for LiveView pages, `curl` or script path for controller/API routes


### Auth

Format:
- Use H2 heading
- Exact commands or instructions the tester copies verbatim

Content:
- Login URL, credentials, headers — whatever the tool needs
- Reference auth scripts from the QA plan if applicable
- Tester should not need to figure out auth on their own


### Seeds

Format:
- Use H2 heading
- Exact commands to run

Content:
- Seed script references (`mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`)
- Any story-specific seed commands beyond the base seeds
- Entity IDs or values the tester will need


### What To Test

Format:
- Use H2 heading
- Bullet list of specific test scenarios

Content:
- Specific URLs to visit
- Interactions to perform (click, fill form, submit)
- Expected outcomes (what the tester should see)
- Map to acceptance criteria from the story


### Result Path

Format:
- Use H2 heading
- Single line: file path

Content:
- Where the tester writes the result document


## Optional Sections

### Setup Notes

Format:
- Use H2 heading
- Free-form paragraphs

Content:
- Additional context, prerequisites, known issues



## Findings and done signal

Every finding you uncover during execution gets filed via
`mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__create_issue` **as you find it** — not
written into a markdown file. Capture the title, severity, scope, and a
short description; the call returns an issue id. Hold those ids.

When you finish the session, call
`mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__submit_qa_result` with the structured
scenarios payload **and** every issue id you filed:

    mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__submit_qa_result(
      task_id: <task_id>,
      status: "pass" | "partial" | "fail",
      scenarios: [%{name: "...", status: "pass|partial|fail", observation: "..."}, ...],
      issue_ids: [<every id returned from create_issue>]
    )

Discipline:

- **`status: "pass"`** with `issue_ids: []` is fine.
- **`status: "partial"` or `"fail"`** with `issue_ids: []` is **rejected
  by the tool**. A failure with no filed issue is a finding that just
  disappeared when your session ended — there's nowhere else for it to
  live. File the issues first, then submit.
- The bare `submit_qa_result` (without the `mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__`
  prefix) does NOT resolve — use the fully-qualified name.
- Don't write findings into a result.md file. The harness doesn't read it.
  Screenshots and other evidence still belong on disk, but the canonical
  record is the DB attempt + linked issues.

short description; the call returns an issue id. Hold those ids.

# QA Plan — Cleaner CRM

## App Overview

Cleaner CRM is a Phoenix 1.8 + LiveView 1.2 app backed by Postgres (Ecto), single OTP release with one endpoint. In dev it listens on **http://127.0.0.1:4100** (`PORT` defaults to 4100 in `config/runtime.exs`; port 4000 is occupied by another app on this machine). Authentication is session-based via phx.gen.auth with magic-link *and* password login at `/users/log-in` (POST `/users/log-in` sets the session cookie; protected routes 302-redirect to the login page when unauthenticated). One router (`CleanerCrmWeb.Router`) with a `:browser` pipeline (CSRF-protected, `fetch_current_scope_for_user`) and a currently-unused `:api` pipeline; authenticated LiveViews live under the `:require_authenticated_user` live_session (`/users/settings`, `/accounts*`, `/integrations`), and domain surfaces (clients, schedule, quotes, invoices, field app) will mount under the same session as they are built. Dev extras: `/dev/dashboard` (LiveDashboard) and `/dev/mailbox` (Swoosh local mailbox — where magic-link and invitation emails land).

## Tools Registry

### Vibium browser (LiveView pages)

Use for anything interactive: LiveView forms, navigation, acknowledgment flows, screenshots. Start with `browser_start`, then `browser_navigate` to `http://127.0.0.1:4100`. Probed login form selectors (REAL, from the rendered page): the login page renders two forms — magic-link first, then password. Password login fields: `input[name="user[email]"]`, `input[name="user[password]"]`, checkbox `input[name="user[remember_me]"]`; CSRF is a hidden `_csrf_token` input handled automatically by form submit. Log in by filling the password form and submitting; success redirects to `/`. Example: `browser_navigate {url: "http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in"}` → `browser_fill {selector: "input[name=\"user[email]\"]", value: "qa-owner@cleanercrm.test"}` → fill password → `browser_click` the password form's submit button.

### curl (controllers, redirects, response codes)

Use for public pages, redirect assertions, and any future JSON/API pipeline. Unauthenticated probe results: `GET /` → 200, `GET /users/log-in` → 200, `GET /users/settings` → 302 (to log-in). Session-authenticated calls: use the wrapper `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh` — it performs the CSRF + cookie login dance (verified working: login POST → 302, `/users/settings` with session → 200). Examples: `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh /users/settings -i` (default owner creds) or `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test "qa password 1234" /accounts -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}"`. Set `BASE_URL` to override the default `http://127.0.0.1:4100`.

### mix run (seeds and one-off setup)

Use to (re)seed QA data: `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` (idempotent). Run the server itself with `mix phx.server` (background); confirm it's up with `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:4100/` → 200. Reset the dev DB entirely with `mix ecto.reset` (drops, recreates, migrates, runs `priv/repo/seeds.exs`), then re-run the QA seeds. Integration credential checks live in `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/verify_*.sh` (stripe, twilio, resend, object_storage, codemyspec) — each prints one-line JSON with `"status": "ok"|"error"`; they need env vars documented in `.code_my_spec/integrations/index.md`.

## Seed Strategy

Single Repo (`CleanerCrm.Repo`, Postgres, dev DB `cleaner_crm_dev`). One QA seed script:

- `priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` — run with `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`. Idempotent (checks by email / existing account before inserting). Creates through real context flows (register → magic-link confirm → set password): **owner** `qa-owner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`, **cleaner** `qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`, and one account **QA Sparkle Cleaning Co** owned by the owner (`Accounts.create_account/2`). Prints credentials and the login URL on completion. Run it after every `mix ecto.reset`, and before any browser session that needs a logged-in user. As domain contexts land (Clients, Scheduling, Quality, …), extend this script with clients/properties/plans rather than adding bash loops — one BEAM boot, all entities.
- `priv/repo/seeds.exs` — stock Phoenix seed file, currently empty; runs automatically during `mix ecto.setup`/`ecto.reset`.

## System Issues

### Port 4000 occupied by another dev app

Another BEAM app on this machine listens on 4000 (and answers `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` with a `dev.codemyspec.com` issuer — it is NOT this app). Cleaner CRM's dev default was moved to **4100** (`config/runtime.exs`, `PORT` env still wins). If a probe of 4000 returns 200s, you are talking to the wrong app. Status: resolved (default port changed).

### `mix test` is rerouted to `mix agent_test`, which skips `ecto.create`

The harness rewrites `mix test`; on a fresh checkout the test DB may not exist and every test fails with `invalid_catalog_name`. Fix: `MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.create && MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.migrate` once. Status: resolved on this machine, will recur on fresh clones.

## Notes

The `:api` pipeline exists but has no routes yet; when API/webhook endpoints land (Stripe webhooks, Twilio status callbacks, reminder confirm links), add curl rows with real headers here. Emails (magic link, invitations) are viewable at `http://127.0.0.1:4100/dev/mailbox` in dev — use it to extract tokens during browser QA. Integration verify scripts are `pending` until the engineer supplies credentials (see `.code_my_spec/integrations/index.md`).

# QA Story Workflow

The `qa_story` agent task is a per-story QA cycle: write a brief, then execute
it against the running app. The project-wide QA plan
(`.code_my_spec/qa/plan.md`) is a prerequisite — produced upstream by
`qa_setup`, not written here.

QA completion is recorded by a DB-backed attempt via `submit_qa_result`. There
is no result.md file in the loop. Findings are filed via `create_issue` as
they're uncovered and linked into the attempt by id.

## Phase 1: Testing brief

**Artifact:** `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/brief.md`

The brief is the concrete plan for testing this story — which tools to use,
how to authenticate, what scenarios to test, and what to assert.

Procedure:

1. Read `.code_my_spec/qa/plan.md` for App Overview, Tools Registry,
   auth strategy, and Seed Strategy.
2. Run seed scripts to verify setup works for this story.
3. If this story needs additional seeds or plan updates, make them now
   and update plan.md (don't fork into a story-specific plan).
4. Read the BDD spec files listed in the prompt. They have selectors,
   test data, and assertions.
5. If a linked component is listed in the prompt, read its source and
   spec to understand the feature.
6. Write the brief to `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/brief.md` matching
   the `qa_story_brief` document spec from the prompt.

## Phase 2: Execute tests

There is no `result.md` artifact in this phase. Findings flow through
`create_issue` as you discover them; the run ends with one call to
`submit_qa_result`.

### Tool rules — pick by Phoenix pipeline, not by guess

- **UI / LiveView (`:browser` pipeline):** MCP browser tools only.
  Navigate, click, type, screenshot. Log in via the browser (credentials
  and login steps are in the plan).
- **API endpoints (`:api` pipeline):** `curl` with API key headers.
  ALWAYS single-line commands. Use
  `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh` for API-key auth.
- **NEVER** use curl with session cookies or CSRF tokens for
  browser-authenticated routes. If a route is behind
  `:require_authenticated_user`, test it with MCP browser tools.

### Testing approach

- Capture a screenshot at each key state (initial load, after
  interactions, success/error states). Save to
  `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/screenshots/`. Screenshots are evidence
  and remain valuable — attach the path in the issue description for
  any finding that ships a screenshot.
- After scripted scenarios, explore freely: unexpected inputs, edge
  cases, empty states, anything that feels off.
- Reference existing scripts in `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/` by path
  rather than inlining shell commands.

### Filing findings

The moment you observe something wrong — a broken UI, a 500, a missing
feature, an unexpected behavior — call `create_issue` and hold the
returned id. Don't accumulate findings in a notepad. Don't write them
into a markdown file. The DB issue is the canonical record.

- `title` — short, scannable.
- `severity` — critical / high / medium / low / info.
- `scope` — `app` for app-under-development bugs; `qa` for QA infrastructure
  problems; `docs` for docs gaps; (`framework` is a server-side concept and
  not selectable from the local list_issues filter, but `create_issue`
  itself supports it for harness issues).
- `story_id` — the story this finding relates to, when relevant.
- `description` — the reproduction, the expected vs actual, file paths,
  and any screenshot or evidence path.

If a finding is a duplicate of an existing issue (you'll see them in the
prompt's "Existing Issues" section), don't refile.

### Procedure

1. Read the brief at `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/brief.md` for the
   complete plan.
2. Read `.code_my_spec/qa/plan.md` for auth strategy and seed commands.
3. Read `priv/knowledge/qa-tooling.md` and `priv/knowledge/qa-tooling/`
   for tool usage patterns.
4. Run seed scripts to set up test data.
5. If a linked component is listed in the prompt, read its source to
   understand implementation details.
6. Execute each test scenario from the brief.
7. Capture screenshots at key states (save to the screenshots directory).
8. For every finding, call `create_issue` immediately and remember the id.
9. If you find a gap in the plan or the brief, fix it in-flight — update

# QA Story Workflow

The `qa_story` agent task is a per-story QA cycle: write a brief, then execute
it against the running app. The project-wide QA plan
(`.code_my_spec/qa/plan.md`) is a prerequisite — produced upstream by
`qa_setup`, not written here.

QA completion is recorded by a DB-backed attempt via `submit_qa_result`. There
is no result.md file in the loop. Findings are filed via `create_issue` as
they're uncovered and linked into the attempt by id.

## Phase 1: Testing brief

**Artifact:** `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/brief.md`

The brief is the concrete plan for testing this story — which tools to use,
how to authenticate, what scenarios to test, and what to assert.

Procedure:

1. Read `.code_my_spec/qa/plan.md` for App Overview, Tools Registry,
   auth strategy, and Seed Strategy.
2. Run seed scripts to verify setup works for this story.
3. If this story needs additional seeds or plan updates, make them now
   and update plan.md (don't fork into a story-specific plan).
4. Read the BDD spec files listed in the prompt. They have selectors,
   test data, and assertions.
5. If a linked component is listed in the prompt, read its source and
   spec to understand the feature.
6. Write the brief to `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/brief.md` matching
   the `qa_story_brief` document spec from the prompt.

`create_issue` as you discover them; the run ends with one call to
`submit_qa_result`.

- **UI / LiveView (`:browser` pipeline):** MCP browser tools only.
  Navigate, click, type, screenshot. Log in via the browser (credentials
  and login steps are in the plan).
- **API endpoints (`:api` pipeline):** `curl` with API key headers.
  ALWAYS single-line commands. Use
  `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh` for API-key auth.
- **NEVER** use curl with session cookies or CSRF tokens for
  browser-authenticated routes. If a route is behind
  `:require_authenticated_user`, test it with MCP browser tools.

  interactions, success/error states). Save to
  `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/screenshots/`. Screenshots are evidence
  and remain valuable — attach the path in the issue description for

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story842.Criterion7160Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 842 — Work each job from a room-by-room checklist with photo proof
  Criterion 7160 — Out-of-scope task is not on the checklist
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "an out-of-scope task never appears on a cleaner's job checklist" do
    scenario "out-of-scope task is not on the checklist" do
      given_(:logged_in_owner_with_account)

      given_ "cleaner Ana is assigned a job whose checklist reflects only what the client agreed to",
             context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{email: "ana@example.com"})

        %{job: job, checklist: checklist} =
          Fixtures.job_with_room_checklist_fixture(context.scope, client, cleaner, [
            %{room: "Kitchen", task: "Kitchen counters wiped down", required: true},
            %{room: "Bathroom", task: "Bathrooms sanitized", required: true}
          ])

        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(build_conn(), cleaner)

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           client: client,
           cleaner: cleaner,
           job: job,
           checklist: checklist,
           conn: conn
         })}
      end

      when_ "Ana opens her job", context do
        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :job_live, job_live)}
      end

      then_ "she sees only the tasks that were agreed to", context do
        assert has_element?(context.job_live, "[data-test='checklist-room-Kitchen']")
        assert has_element?(context.job_live, "[data-test='checklist-room-Bathroom']")

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "an add-on task the client declined, such as oven interior cleaning, is not on the checklist",
            context do
        refute render(context.job_live) =~ "Inside oven cleaned"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story842.Criterion7172Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 842 — Work each job from a room-by-room checklist with photo proof
  Criterion 7172 — Photo taken offline uploads when signal returns
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a checklist photo captured with no signal finishes uploading once connectivity returns" do
    scenario "photo taken offline uploads when signal returns" do
      given_(:logged_in_owner_with_account)

      given_ "cleaner Ana is logged in on her assigned job with a checklist", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{email: "ana@example.com"})

        %{job: job, checklist: checklist} =
          Fixtures.job_with_checklist_fixture(context.scope, client, cleaner)

        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(build_conn(), cleaner)

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           client: client,
           cleaner: cleaner,
           job: job,
           checklist: checklist,
           conn: conn
         })}
      end

      when_ "Ana captures the after photo of the first task while her phone has no signal",
            context do
        [task | _] = context.checklist.items

        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        upload =
          file_input(
            job_live,
            "[data-test='task-#{task.id}-after-photo-form']",
            :after_photo,
            [
              %{
                name: "after_kitchen.jpg",
                content: String.duplicate("a", 100),
                type: "image/jpeg"
              }
            ]
          )

        render_upload(upload, "after_kitchen.jpg", 40)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{job_live: job_live, task: task, upload: upload})}
      end

      then_ "the photo sits queued as a pending upload", context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.job_live,
                 "[data-test='task-#{context.task.id}-photo-pending']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "her signal returns", context do
        render_upload(context.upload, "after_kitchen.jpg", 60)

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the photo finishes uploading and is attached to the task", context do
        refute has_element?(
                 context.job_live,
                 "[data-test='task-#{context.task.id}-photo-pending']"
               )

        assert has_element?(
                 context.job_live,
                 "[data-test='task-#{context.task.id}-after-photo']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

# QA Story 843: Get loud, acknowledged alerts when my schedule changes

Run a full QA session for this story. Two phases: write a testing brief,
then execute it. The playbook below has the detailed procedure.

**App URL:** Run `mix run -e 'IO.puts(CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url())'`.

## Story description

As a cleaner, I want schedule changes (added/moved/cancelled jobs) pushed to me as notifications that I explicitly acknowledge — with the office seeing unacknowledged changes — so that mid-day changes actually reach me and same-day cleanings aren't silently missed. (Research: undelivered assignment changes are the most common cause of missed same-day cleanings — pain-points §2.4)

## Acceptance criteria

- Moved job notifies the cleaner
- Cancelled job notifies the cleaner
- Acknowledging clears the pending change
- Unacknowledged change keeps prompting
- Office sees who has not acknowledged
- Never-acknowledged same-day change escalates
- Push failure falls back to SMS

=== criterion_7190_moved_job_notifies_the_cleaner_spex ===
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story843.Criterion7190Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 843 — Get loud, acknowledged alerts when my schedule changes
  Criterion 7190 — Moving a job's time on the schedule board pushes the
  reassigned cleaner a notification describing the old and new times.

  Assumes the board exposes a per-job start-time control
  (`[data-test='job-<id>-start-time-input']`, `phx-change="reschedule_job"`)
  alongside the cleaner-select control already assumed by story 834's
  criterion 7170.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a moved job notifies the assigned cleaner" do
    scenario "moved job notifies the cleaner" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "I am a cleaner with a job scheduled today at 1:00 PM", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "cleaner-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        cleaner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn(), cleaner)
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
            start_time: ~T[13:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[14:30:00]
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaner: cleaner, cleaner_conn: cleaner_conn, job: job})}

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.Index do @moduledoc """ Weekly board of every cleaner's schedule, with unassigned jobs called out separately, inline reassignment, and inline job creation/editing/rescheduling/cancellation per job. Route: `/schedule`. Always shows the week containing today — there is no week navigation yet. """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job alias CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponent @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H""" <.header> Weekly Schedule <:subtitle>{length(@jobs)} jobs scheduled <:actions> <.button data-test="new-job-button" phx-click="new_job" variant="primary"> New Job

That reassignment conflicts with the cleaner's availability or another booking.

This visit is now assigned away from the client's preferred cleaner.

<.live_component module={JobFormComponent} id="new-job-form" current_scope={@current_scope} action={:quick_new} job={%Job{start_time: ~T[09:00:00], end_time: ~T[11:00:00]}} />

{cleaner.name || cleaner.email}

<.job_card :for={job <- jobs_for_cleaner(@jobs, cleaner.id)} job={job} cleaners={@cleaners} current_scope={@current_scope} editing_job_id={@editing_job_id} />

Unassigned

<.job_card :for={job <- unassigned_jobs(@jobs)} job={job} cleaners={@cleaners} current_scope={@current_scope} editing_job_id={@editing_job_id} />
""" end attr :job, :map, required: true attr :cleaners, :list, required: true attr :current_scope, :map, required: true attr :editing_job_id, :string, default: nil defp job_card(assigns) do ~H"""
<.live_component module={JobFormComponent} id={"edit-job-#{@job.id}"} current_scope={@current_scope} action={:edit} job={@job} />
{@job.scheduled_date}
- {@job.end_time}
{reminder_status_label(status)}
{@job.property.service_address}
Lockbox: {@job.property.lockbox_code}
Parking: {@job.property.parking_notes}
Pets: {@job.property.pet_notes}
{ack_status_label(alert)} {channel_label(alert)} - {alert.change_summary}
""" end @impl true def mount(_params, _session, socket) do week_start = week_start(Date.utc_today()) {:ok, socket |> assign(:week_start, week_start) |> assign(:conflict_warning, nil) |> assign(:preferred_cleaner_warning, false) |> assign(:show_new_job_form, false) |> assign(:editing_job_id, nil) |> load_week()} end @impl true def handle_event("new_job", _params, socket) do {:noreply, assign(socket, :show_new_job_form, true)} end def handle_event("reassign_job:" <> job_id, %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job_id) case Scheduling.assign_cleaner(scope, job, parse_id(cleaner_id)) do {:ok, updated} -> if updated.cleaner_id do notify_schedule_change( scope, updated, "Assigned to job on #{updated.scheduled_date} at #{format_time_12h(updated.start_time)}" ) end {:noreply, socket |> assign(:conflict_warning, nil) |> assign(:preferred_cleaner_warning, deviates_from_preferred_cleaner?(scope, updated)) |> load_week()} {:error, _reason} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :conflict_warning, true)} end end def handle_event("edit_job:" <> job_id, _params, socket) do {:noreply, assign(socket, :editing_job_id, job_id)} end def handle_event("cancel_job:" <> job_id, _params, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job_id) {:ok, _updated} = Scheduling.cancel_job(scope, job) notify_schedule_change(scope, job, "Cancelled") {:noreply, load_week(socket)} end def handle_event("delete_job:" <> job_id, _params, socket) do job = Scheduling.get_job!(socket.assigns.current_scope, job_id) {:ok, _updated} = Scheduling.delete_job(socket.assigns.current_scope, job) {:noreply, load_week(socket)} end def handle_event("reschedule_job:" <> job_id, %{"start_time" => start_time}, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job_id) new_start = parse_time(start_time) new_end = Time.add(new_start, Time.diff(job.end_time, job.start_time), :second) case Scheduling.update_job(scope, job, %{start_time: new_start, end_time: new_end}) do {:ok, _updated} -> notify_schedule_change( scope, job, "Job moved from #{format_time_12h(job.start_time)} to #{format_time_12h(new_start)}" ) {:noreply, load_week(socket)} {:error, _changeset} -> {:noreply, socket} end end @impl true def handle_info({JobFormComponent, {:job_created, _job}}, socket) do {:noreply, socket |> assign(:show_new_job_form, false) |> load_week()} end def handle_info({JobFormComponent, {:job_updated, _job}}, socket) do {:noreply, socket |> assign(:editing_job_id, nil) |> load_week()} end defp load_week(socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope socket |> assign(:jobs, Scheduling.list_jobs(scope)) |> assign(:cleaners, Scheduling.list_cleaners(scope)) end # Story 846: a job materialized from a recurring plan carries that # plan's preferred cleaner as its default assignment (see # `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.job_attrs/1`). Reassigning it to # someone else always succeeds — this only flags the deviation for # the owner, it's a warning, never a block. A one-off job (no # `recurring_plan_id`) or a plan with no preference set (`cleaner_id` # nil) never warns, since there's nothing to deviate from. defp deviates_from_preferred_cleaner?(_scope, %Job{recurring_plan_id: nil}), do: false defp deviates_from_preferred_cleaner?(scope, %Job{} = job) do plan = Scheduling.get_recurring_plan!(scope, job.recurring_plan_id) not is_nil(plan.cleaner_id) and plan.cleaner_id != job.cleaner_id end defp week_start(date), do: Date.add(date, -(Date.day_of_week(date) - 1)) defp jobs_for_cleaner(jobs, cleaner_id), do: Enum.filter(jobs, &(&1.cleaner_id == cleaner_id)) defp unassigned_jobs(jobs), do: Enum.filter(jobs, &is_nil(&1.cleaner_id)) defp parse_id(""), do: nil defp parse_id(nil), do: nil defp parse_id(id) when is_binary(id), do: String.to_integer(id) defp parse_time(str) when byte_size(str) == 5, do: Time.from_iso8601!(str <> ":00") defp parse_time(str), do: Time.from_iso8601!(str) # `CleanerCrm.Notifications` owns the per-job schedule-change alert # (acknowledgment status, fallback channel) and the client's # reminder confirm/reschedule decision. Read both defensively — # `function_exported?` rather than a direct call — so this file # tolerates that context landing or changing shape independently of # the board. defp notifications_ready?(fun, arity), do: Code.ensure_loaded?(CleanerCrm.Notifications) and function_exported?(CleanerCrm.Notifications, fun, arity) # Expected contract: `latest_schedule_change_for_job(scope, job_id)` # returns `nil` or something map-like with `:status` # (`:pending` | `:acknowledged` | `:escalated`) and `:channel` # (`:push` | `:sms` | `:email`) keys, matching # `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.schedule_change_notification_fixture/4`'s # shape. defp schedule_change_alert(scope, job) do if notifications_ready?(:latest_schedule_change_for_job, 2) do CleanerCrm.Notifications.latest_schedule_change_for_job(scope, job.id) end end defp ack_status_label(%{status: :pending}), do: "Unacknowledged" defp ack_status_label(%{status: :acknowledged}), do: "Acknowledged" defp ack_status_label(%{status: :escalated}), do: "Escalated" defp ack_status_label(_alert), do: "Unacknowledged" defp channel_label(%{channel: :push}), do: "Push" defp channel_label(%{channel: :sms}), do: "SMS" defp channel_label(%{channel: :email}), do: "Email" defp channel_label(_alert), do: "Push" # Expected contract: `reminder_status_for_job(job_id)` returns `nil` # (no decision yet), `:confirmed`, or `:reschedule_requested` — the # client's most recent decision on their appointment reminder. defp reminder_status(job) do if notifications_ready?(:reminder_status_for_job, 1) do CleanerCrm.Notifications.reminder_status_for_job(job.id) end end defp reminder_status_label(:confirmed), do: "Confirmed" defp reminder_status_label(:reschedule_requested), do: "Needs reschedule" defp reminder_status_label(_status), do: nil # Composes the cleaner-facing schedule-change alert on a reschedule # or cancellation. This is the sanctioned place for it, not # `CleanerCrm.Scheduling`: the dependency graph has # `Notifications -> Scheduling`, so `Scheduling` itself must never # call back into `Notifications` — this LiveView is what's allowed # to depend on both and compose them. No-ops for an unassigned job # (nobody to notify) or if `Notifications` isn't loaded yet. defp notify_schedule_change(scope, job, change_summary) do if job.cleaner_id && notifications_ready?(:create_notification, 2) do cleaner = Enum.find(Scheduling.list_cleaners(scope), &(&1.id == job.cleaner_id)) CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(scope, %{ cleaner_id: job.cleaner_id, job_id: job.id, kind: :schedule_change, channel: notification_channel(cleaner), status: :pending, change_summary: change_summary, pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(), token: "schedule_change_#{job.id}_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}" }) end end # Falls back to SMS when the cleaner has push notifications # disabled. There's no such preference on `CleanerCrm.Users.User` # yet, so this is currently always `:push` — matched defensively so # it starts honoring the preference the moment that field lands, # with no further change needed here. defp notification_channel(%{push_enabled: false}), do: :sms defp notification_channel(_cleaner), do: :push defp format_time_12h(%Time{} = time) do {hour, period} = to_12_hour(time.hour) "#{hour}:#{time.minute |> Integer.to_string() |> String.pad_leading(2, "0")} #{period}" end defp to_12_hour(0), do: {12, "AM"} defp to_12_hour(hour) when hour < 12, do: {hour, "AM"} defp to_12_hour(12), do: {12, "PM"} defp to_12_hour(hour), do: {hour - 12, "PM"} end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications do
  @moduledoc """
  Client appointment reminders with confirm/reschedule actions, and
  cleaner schedule-change alerts requiring explicit acknowledgment with
  office visibility into what's still unacknowledged. Email/SMS
  delivery is abstracted behind `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery`.

  Most functions are scoped by the caller's `Scope`. The confirm,
  reschedule, and delivery-status webhook endpoints are reached by an
  unauthenticated client or provider, so they look a notification up by
  its opaque `token` (or the provider's message id) instead.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{
    Notification,
    ReminderNotifier,
    ReminderScheduler,
    ReminderSettings
  }

  ## Reminder settings

  @doc "The account's reminder settings, defaulting to a 24-hour lead time if never configured."
  def get_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(ReminderSettings, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id}
      settings -> settings
    end
  end

  def change_reminder_settings(%Scope{} = scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope |> get_reminder_settings() |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
  end

  def update_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_reminder_settings()
    |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end

  @doc "Runs the periodic reminder scan now — see `CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler`."
  defdelegate send_due_reminders(), to: ReminderScheduler, as: :scan_and_send

  ## Notifications

  def create_notification(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Notification{account_id: account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc "The office's delivery log: every notification for the account, most recent first."
  def list_notifications(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> preload([:client, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Public confirm/reschedule — reached by token, no scope available

  def get_notification_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    Repo.get_by(Notification, token: token)
  end

  def confirm_reminder(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification, status: :confirmed, confirmed_at: DateTime.utc_now())
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  def request_reschedule(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification,
        status: :reschedule_requested,
        reschedule_requested_at: DateTime.utc_now()
      )
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc "True once the client has confirmed the most recent reminder sent for this job."
  def job_confirmed?(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :confirmed)
    |> Repo.exists?()
  end

  @doc "True once the client has asked to reschedule via the most recent reminder for this job."
  def reschedule_requested?(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :reschedule_requested
    )
    |> Repo.exists?()
  end

  @doc """
  The client's confirm/reschedule decision on their most recent
  reminder for this job, for `ScheduleLive.Index` to render on the
  board — `nil` (no decision yet), `:confirmed`, or
  `:reschedule_requested`.
  """
  def reminder_status_for_job(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder)
    |> where([n], n.status in [:confirmed, :reschedule_requested])
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> select([n], n.status)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  ## Twilio delivery-status webhook

  @doc """
  Applies a Twilio status callback: marks the matching notification
  delivered or undelivered, and — for an undeliverable SMS reminder —
  falls back to emailing the client and flags it for office visibility.
  """
  def handle_delivery_status(%{"MessageSid" => sid, "MessageStatus" => status} = params)
      when is_binary(sid) do
    # Most-recent match: real SIDs are unique, but webhook retries racing
    # inserts (or duplicated test data) must not 500 the endpoint.
    notification =
      from(n in Notification,
        where: n.provider_message_id == ^sid,
        order_by: [desc: n.inserted_at],
        limit: 1
      )
      |> Repo.one()

    case notification do
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
      notification -> apply_delivery_status(notification, status, params["ErrorCode"])
    end
  end

  def handle_delivery_status(_params), do: {:error, :invalid_payload}

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, "delivered", _error_code) do
    update_status(notification, status: :delivered, delivered_at: DateTime.utc_now())
  end

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, status, error_code)
       when status in ["failed", "undelivered"] do
    with {:ok, updated} <-
           update_status(notification, status: :undelivered, failure_reason: error_code || status) do
      maybe_fallback_to_email(updated)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, _status, _error_code), do: {:ok, notification}

  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(
         %Notification{kind: :reminder, channel: :sms, client_id: client_id} = notification
       )
       when not is_nil(client_id) do
    client = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, notification.client_id)
    job = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, notification.job_id)
    token = generate_token()

    confirm_url = reminder_url("/reminders/confirm/#{token}")
    reschedule_url = reminder_url("/reminders/reschedule/#{token}")

    {:ok, _email} = ReminderNotifier.deliver_reminder(client, job, confirm_url, reschedule_url)

    %Notification{account_id: notification.account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(%{
      client_id: client.id,
      job_id: job.id,
      kind: :reminder,
      channel: :email,
      status: :sent,
      token: token,
      sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(_notification), do: :ok

  ## Schedule-change alerts (story 843 groundwork)

  def acknowledge(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification, status: :acknowledged, acknowledged_at: DateTime.utc_now())
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc "Pending schedule-change alerts a cleaner hasn't acknowledged yet, for office visibility."
  def list_unacknowledged(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.account_id == ^account_id and n.kind == :schedule_change and n.status == :pending
    )
    |> preload([:cleaner, :job])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  The most recent schedule-change alert pushed for this job — `nil`,
  or a `Notification` exposing `:status`
  (`:pending` | `:acknowledged` | `:escalated`) and `:channel`
  (`:push` | `:sms` | `:email`). This is the contract
  `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.Index` reads defensively to show a job's
  ack status on the board.
  """
  def latest_schedule_change_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, job_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.account_id == ^account_id and n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :schedule_change
    )
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
    |> maybe_escalate()
  end

  # A same-day change nobody has acknowledged within the escalation
  # window re-sends via the fallback channel (SMS) and flags as
  # escalated for office visibility. Computed on read rather than a
  # separate periodic pass — every read of a job's alert (the board,
  # `FieldLive.Today`) goes through here, so none of them can show a
  # stale "pending" past the window.
  @escalation_window_seconds 600

  defp maybe_escalate(%Notification{status: :pending} = notification) do
    if escalation_due?(notification) do
      {:ok, updated} =
        update_status(notification,
          status: :escalated,
          channel: :sms,
          escalated_at: DateTime.utc_now()
        )

      updated
    else
      notification
    end
  end

  defp maybe_escalate(notification), do: notification

  defp escalation_due?(%Notification{pushed_at: nil}), do: false

  defp escalation_due?(%Notification{pushed_at: pushed_at, job_id: job_id}) do
    job = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, job_id)

    Date.compare(job.scheduled_date, Date.utc_today()) != :gt and
      DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(), pushed_at, :second) >= @escalation_window_seconds
  end

  ## Shared helpers

  @doc false
  def generate_token, do: Base.url_encode64(:crypto.strong_rand_bytes(24), padding: false)

  defp update_status(%Notification{} = notification, attrs) do
    notification
    |> Notification.changeset(Map.new(attrs))
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  # `CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url()` is the standard phx.gen.auth-style
  # exception for building absolute links in outbound messages — see
  # the `dirty_xrefs` note on the `CleanerCrm` boundary.
  defp reminder_url(path), do: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> path
end

  end

  def request_reschedule(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification,
        status: :reschedule_requested,
        reschedule_requested_at: DateTime.utc_now()
      )
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc "True once the client has confirmed the most recent reminder sent for this job."
  def job_confirmed?(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :confirmed)
    |> Repo.exists?()
  end

  @doc "True once the client has asked to reschedule via the most recent reminder for this job."
  def reschedule_requested?(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :reschedule_requested
    )
    |> Repo.exists?()
  end

  @doc """
  The client's confirm/reschedule decision on their most recent
  reminder for this job, for `ScheduleLive.Index` to render on the
  board — `nil` (no decision yet), `:confirmed`, or
  `:reschedule_requested`.
  """
  def reminder_status_for_job(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder)
    |> where([n], n.status in [:confirmed, :reschedule_requested])
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> select([n], n.status)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  ## Twilio delivery-status webhook

  @doc """
  Applies a Twilio status callback: marks the matching notification
  delivered or undelivered, and — for an undeliverable SMS reminder —
  falls back to emailing the client and flags it for office visibility.
  """
  def handle_delivery_status(%{"MessageSid" => sid, "MessageStatus" => status} = params)
      when is_binary(sid) do
    # Most-recent match: real SIDs are unique, but webhook retries racing
    # inserts (or duplicated test data) must not 500 the endpoint.
    notification =
      from(n in Notification,
        where: n.provider_message_id == ^sid,
        order_by: [desc: n.inserted_at],
        limit: 1
      )
      |> Repo.one()

    case notification do
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
      notification -> apply_delivery_status(notification, status, params["ErrorCode"])
    end
  end

  def handle_delivery_status(_params), do: {:error, :invalid_payload}

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, "delivered", _error_code) do
    update_status(notification, status: :delivered, delivered_at: DateTime.utc_now())
  end

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, status, error_code)
       when status in ["failed", "undelivered"] do
    with {:ok, updated} <-
           update_status(notification, status: :undelivered, failure_reason: error_code || status) do
      maybe_fallback_to_email(updated)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, _status, _error_code), do: {:ok, notification}

  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(
         %Notification{kind: :reminder, channel: :sms, client_id: client_id} = notification
       )
       when not is_nil(client_id) do
    client = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, notification.client_id)
    job = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, notification.job_id)
    token = generate_token()

    confirm_url = reminder_url("/reminders/confirm/#{token}")
    reschedule_url = reminder_url("/reminders/reschedule/#{token}")

    {:ok, _email} = ReminderNotifier.deliver_reminder(client, job, confirm_url, reschedule_url)

    %Notification{account_id: notification.account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(%{
      client_id: client.id,
      job_id: job.id,
      kind: :reminder,
      channel: :email,
      status: :sent,
      token: token,
      sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(_notification), do: :ok

  ## Schedule-change alerts (story 843 groundwork)

  def acknowledge(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification, status: :acknowledged, acknowledged_at: DateTime.utc_now())
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc "Pending schedule-change alerts a cleaner hasn't acknowledged yet, for office visibility."
  def list_unacknowledged(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.account_id == ^account_id and n.kind == :schedule_change and n.status == :pending
    )
    |> preload([:cleaner, :job])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  The most recent schedule-change alert pushed for this job — `nil`,
  or a `Notification` exposing `:status`
  (`:pending` | `:acknowledged` | `:escalated`) and `:channel`
  (`:push` | `:sms` | `:email`). This is the contract
  `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.Index` reads defensively to show a job's
  ack status on the board.
  """
  def latest_schedule_change_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, job_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.account_id == ^account_id and n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :schedule_change
    )
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
    |> maybe_escalate()
  end

  # A same-day change nobody has acknowledged within the escalation
  # window re-sends via the fallback channel (SMS) and flags as
  # escalated for office visibility. Computed on read rather than a
  # separate periodic pass — every read of a job's alert (the board,
  # `FieldLive.Today`) goes through here, so none of them can show a
  # stale "pending" past the window.
  @escalation_window_seconds 600

  defp maybe_escalate(%Notification{status: :pending} = notification) do
    if escalation_due?(notification) do
      {:ok, updated} =
        update_status(notification,
          status: :escalated,
          channel: :sms,
          escalated_at: DateTime.utc_now()
        )

      updated
    else
      notification
    end
  end

  defp maybe_escalate(notification), do: notification

  defp escalation_due?(%Notification{pushed_at: nil}), do: false

  defp escalation_due?(%Notification{pushed_at: pushed_at, job_id: job_id}) do
    job = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, job_id)

    Date.compare(job.scheduled_date, Date.utc_today()) != :gt and
      DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(), pushed_at, :second) >= @escalation_window_seconds
  end

  ## Shared helpers

  @doc false
  def generate_token, do: Base.url_encode64(:crypto.strong_rand_bytes(24), padding: false)

  defp update_status(%Notification{} = notification, attrs) do
    notification
    |> Notification.changeset(Map.new(attrs))
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  # `CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url()` is the standard phx.gen.auth-style
  # exception for building absolute links in outbound messages — see
  # the `dirty_xrefs` note on the `CleanerCrm` boundary.
  defp reminder_url(path), do: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> path
end

# Qa Story Brief — 843 Get loud, acknowledged alerts when my schedule changes

## Tool

web

## Auth

Two sessions needed in the same browser (log in/out between phases as needed):
- Owner: `qa-owner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234` via `/users/log-in` (password form).
- Cleaner: `qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`, same form.

## Seeds

Uses existing fixture jobs (both `scheduled`, today 2026-07-08, assigned to qa-cleaner, user id 2):
- Job A `7a048bd4-c474-4d50-a4bd-7e5bdc74f27d` — 836 Card St, 13:00-15:00. Used for the moved-job / acknowledge / push-fallback scenarios.
- Job B `dbd5a7b7-5390-423f-9fab-ca100cdcced8` — 475 QA841 Test Ave, 11:00-12:00. Used for the cancel / keeps-prompting / escalation scenarios.

Escalation window is 600s, computed lazily on every read (`CleanerCrm.Notifications.latest_schedule_change_for_job/2`) — no periodic job to wait for; pin `pushed_at` via psql to simulate elapsed time:
`psql -h localhost -d cleaner_crm_dev -c "update notifications set pushed_at = now() - interval '11 minutes' where job_id = 'dbd5a7b7-5390-423f-9fab-ca100cdcced8' and status = 'pending';"`

Push-fallback needs `push_enabled = false` on the cleaner (no UI toggle exists yet):
`psql -h localhost -d cleaner_crm_dev -c "update users set push_enabled = false where email = 'qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test';"`
Revert after testing: `... set push_enabled = true where email = ...`.

## What To Test

- Owner on `/schedule`: change Job A's `[data-test='job-<id>-start-time-input']` to a new time → board's `[data-test='job-<id>-ack-status']` shows "Unacknowledged" and `[data-test='job-<id>-notification-channel']` shows "Push" + the new time.
- Cleaner on `/field`: sees `[data-test='schedule-alert']` with both old and new times in the message.
- Cleaner clicks `[data-test='schedule-alert-<id>-acknowledge-button']` → alert disappears; reload `/field` → still gone.
- Owner reloads `/schedule` → Job A's ack-status flips to "Acknowledged".
- Owner cancels Job B via `[data-test='job-<id>-cancel-button']` → cleaner's `/field` shows an alert containing "Cancelled".
- Without acknowledging, reload cleaner's `/field` again → the same alert is still present (unacknowledged change keeps prompting).
- Pin Job B's notification `pushed_at` 11 minutes back via the psql command above → owner reloads `/schedule` → Job B's ack-status shows "Escalated" and channel shows "SMS".
- Set `push_enabled=false` on qa-cleaner, reschedule Job A to a further new time → board's notification-channel for Job A shows "SMS" + the new time (push failure fallback). Revert `push_enabled` to true afterward.

## Result Path

No result.md — findings via `create_issue`, outcome via `submit_qa_result`.

## Setup Notes

`schedule_change_alert/2` reads the *latest* notification per job, so re-triggering a change on the same job (e.g. Job A twice) always reflects the newest one — expected, not a bug. Office routes are owner-only; cleaner routes are `/field*`.

content.text: This is a meaningful finding: cancelling a job removes it entirely from the schedule board's job list, which means the office loses all visibility into that job's schedule-change acknowledgment status, and the escalation check (which only runs when the board reads a job's latest notification) can never fire for it. Let me file this.

input.title: Cancelled job's schedule-change notification is invisible to the office and can never escalate
input.description:
Reproduction: as owner on /schedule, cancel a cleaner's job via [data-test='job-<id>-cancel-button']. A schedule_change notification (kind=schedule_change, status=pending, channel=push, summary="Cancelled") is correctly created and the cleaner sees the "Cancelled" alert on /field (confirmed via psql + browser).

However, `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.list_jobs/1` (lib/cleaner_crm/scheduling.ex:143) filters `where j.status != :cancelled`, so a cancelled job's row (and its `[data-test='job-<id>-ack-status']` / `[data-test='job-<id>-notification-channel']` indicators) disappears from ScheduleLive.Index entirely the moment it's cancelled.

Two consequences, both against story 843's acceptance criteria:
1. "Office sees who has not acknowledged" fails specifically for cancellations: there is no way for the office to see whether the cleaner has acknowledged a job cancellation, since the board never renders that job's row again.
2. "Never-acknowledged same-day change escalates" never fires for cancellations: `CleanerCrm.Notifications.maybe_escalate/1` (lib/cleaner_crm/notifications.ex) — the function that flips a stale pending notification to :escalated and re-sends via SMS — is only invoked from `latest_schedule_change_for_job/2`, which is only ever called by ScheduleLive.Index.schedule_change_alert/2 for jobs in `@jobs`. Since cancelled jobs are excluded from that list, a cancellation notification can sit `pending` forever with no escalation check ever running, no matter how long it goes unacknowledged.

This is arguably the highest-stakes case for the whole story: a cleaner who never sees/acknowledges that their job was cancelled might show up anyway, and the office has no way to notice the unacknowledged cancellation because the row is gone.

Expected: the office should still be able to see acknowledgment status (and escalation) for a cancelled job's schedule-change notification, e.g. by not filtering cancelled jobs out of the board (or showing them in a distinct "cancelled" section) at least while they carry an unacknowledged/escalated notification.

Verified via: browser session as qa-owner/qa-cleaner, job dbd5a7b7-5390-423f-9fab-ca100cdcced8, and psql confirming the notification row (id 5dd646b7-e1d6-450b-9734-a2395e66cd2a) stays status=pending indefinitely with no escalation path reachable.

scenarios.name: Acknowledging clears the pending change
scenarios.observation: Clicking Acknowledge on Job A's alert removed it immediately and it stayed gone after a fresh reload of /field; office board's ack-status for that job flipped from Unacknowledged to Acknowledged.

scenarios.name: Unacknowledged change keeps prompting
scenarios.observation: Reloading /field without acknowledging (tested on both the moved-job and cancelled-job alerts) kept showing the same schedule-alert on every subsequent load.

scenarios.name: Office sees who has not acknowledged
scenarios.observation: Works correctly for a moved/reassigned job (ack-status visible and flips Unacknowledged->Acknowledged on the board). Fails for a cancelled job: Scheduling.list_jobs/1 excludes cancelled jobs, so the job's row (and its ack-status/notification-channel) disappears from /schedule entirely the moment it's cancelled -- the office has no way to see whether a cancellation was acknowledged. Filed as issue 7df52070-dc5a-49fc-b3ac-925cecce6f3d.

scenarios.name: Never-acknowledged same-day change escalates
scenarios.observation: Works correctly for a moved job: pinning pushed_at 11 minutes back (past the 600s window) flipped the board's ack-status to 'Escalated' and channel to 'SMS' on next read. Root-caused the same way as the cancelled-job gap above: escalation is computed lazily inside latest_schedule_change_for_job/2, only ever called by the board for jobs still in list_jobs/1 -- so a cancelled job's notification can never reach the escalation check and will sit pending forever. Same issue id: 7df52070-dc5a-49fc-b3ac-925cecce6f3d.

scenarios.name: Push failure falls back to SMS
scenarios.observation: With push_enabled=false set via psql on qa-cleaner, rescheduling Job A produced a fresh notification whose board channel showed 'SMS - Job moved from 4:00 PM to 5:00 PM' immediately (no escalation wait needed). push_enabled reverted to true afterward for later stories.

# QA Story 844: Clock in/out per job and see my earnings build

Run a full QA session for this story. Two phases: write a testing brief,
then execute it. The playbook below has the detailed procedure.

**App URL:** Run `mix run -e 'IO.puts(CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url())'`.

## Story description

As a cleaner, I want to clock in/out on each job (or see its piece-rate) and watch my per-job and pay-period earnings accumulate transparently, so that I trust I'm being paid for all my work including drive time policies I can see. (Research: pay opacity and unpaid drive time breed distrust; pay transparency is the stickiest cleaner feature — pain-points §2.3)

## Acceptance criteria

- Cleaner clocks in to their assigned job
- Cleaner cannot clock in to a job assigned to someone else
- Clocking in to a second job while already clocked in
- Clock out then clock in to the next job
- Hourly job earnings computed from clocked time
- Piece-rate job shows its fixed rate up front
- Running pay-period total grows as jobs complete
- Cleaner sees the drive-time policy with their earnings

=== criterion_7126_cleaner_clocks_in_to_their_assigned_job_spex ===
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story844.Criterion7126Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 844 — Clock in/out per job and see my earnings build
  Criterion 7126 — Cleaner clocks in to their assigned job
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a cleaner clocks in to their own assigned job" do
    scenario "cleaner clocks in to their assigned job" do
      given_ "the owner has an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "I am a cleaner assigned to today's 9:00 AM job at the Smith home", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "cleaner-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{name: "Smith"})

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            status: :scheduled
          })

        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, cleaner)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaner: cleaner, job: job, conn: conn})}
      end

      when_ "I open that job and tap Clock In", context do
        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        job_live
        |> element("[data-test='clock-in-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :job_live, job_live)}
      end

      then_ "I am clocked in", context do
        assert render(context.job_live) =~ "Clocked in"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the job shows a running elapsed time starting now", context do
        assert has_element?(context.job_live, "[data-test='elapsed-time']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story844.Criterion7129Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 844 — Clock in/out per job and see my earnings build
  Criterion 7129 — Cleaner cannot clock in to a job assigned to someone else

  Reconciled with story 838 criterion 7123: opening a job assigned to
  someone else redirects away entirely (the job page exposes entry codes,
  so unassigned cleaners must not see it at all). "Cannot clock in"
  follows from "cannot open".
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a cleaner cannot start time on a job assigned to someone else" do
    scenario "cleaner cannot clock in to a job assigned to someone else" do
      given_ "the owner has an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a job at the Jones home is assigned to another cleaner, not me", context do
        other_cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "other-cleaner-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        me =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "me-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{name: "Jones"})

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: other_cleaner.id,
            status: :scheduled
          })

        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, me)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{me: me, job: job, conn: conn})}
      end

      when_ "I attempt to open that job", context do
        {:error, {:redirect, %{to: path, flash: flash}}} =
          live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{redirect_path: path, redirect_flash: flash})}
      end

      then_ "I am redirected away and cannot see the job at all", context do
        assert context.redirect_path == ~p"/field"
        assert context.redirect_flash["error"] =~ "not assigned"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "I cannot start time on it", context do
        refute Map.has_key?(context, :job_live)

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

      when_ "I view my earnings summary", context do
        {:ok, field_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field")

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{field_live: field_live, html: html})}
      end

      then_ "the drive-time policy is stated plainly", context do
        downcased = String.downcase(context.html)

        assert downcased =~ "drive time"

        assert has_element?(context.field_live, "[data-test='drive-time-policy']")

        {:ok, context}
      end

---
defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings do
  @moduledoc """
  Pure pay calculations — no scope, no `Repo`. Given a job and its
  time entries, this is the only place clocked time (or a fixed piece
  rate) turns into cents.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.TimeEntry

  @doc "Seconds between clock-in and clock-out. Only meaningful once resolved."
  def worked_seconds(%TimeEntry{clocked_in_at: in_at, clocked_out_at: out_at})
      when not is_nil(out_at) do
    DateTime.diff(out_at, in_at, :second)
  end

  @doc "Seconds elapsed so far on a still-open entry."
  def elapsed_seconds(%TimeEntry{clocked_out_at: nil, clocked_in_at: in_at}) do
    DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(), in_at, :second)
  end

  @doc """
  Cents earned on a job given its (possibly empty) list of time
  entries: the flat piece rate regardless of time for a piece-rate job
  — shown even before the cleaner has started, since it doesn't
  depend on any entry existing — or the hourly rate times total
  resolved worked time. `nil` when an hourly job has no resolved
  entries yet, or a job carries neither pay type: there's nothing to
  compute pay from, and it must not be silently priced at $0.
  """
  def job_cents(%Job{pay_type: :piece_rate, piece_rate_cents: cents}, _entries)
      when is_integer(cents) do
    cents
  end

  def job_cents(%Job{pay_type: :hourly, hourly_rate_cents: rate}, entries)
      when is_integer(rate) and is_list(entries) and entries != [] do
    if Enum.all?(entries, &TimeEntry.resolved?/1) do
      entries |> Enum.map(&worked_seconds/1) |> Enum.sum() |> hourly_cents(rate)
    end
  end

  def job_cents(_job, _entries), do: nil

  defp hourly_cents(seconds, rate_cents) do
    Decimal.new(rate_cents)
    |> Decimal.mult(Decimal.div(Decimal.new(seconds), Decimal.new(3600)))
    |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up)
    |> Decimal.to_integer()
  end
end

# Qa Story Brief — 844 Clock in/out per job and see my earnings build

## Tool

web

## Auth

Cleaner: `qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234` via `/users/log-in` (password form). One scenario also needs the owner session (`qa-owner@cleanercrm.test`, same password) only to confirm a different cleaner's job id; no owner-side UI assertions are required for this story.

## Seeds

Existing/added fixtures, all under account `QA Sparkle Cleaning Co` (`b4ecfdf7-95d9-4fc0-884a-353d9db1c473`), cleaner qa-cleaner (user id 2):

- Job `7a048bd4-c474-4d50-a4bd-7e5bdc74f27d` — piece-rate, `$80.00` (`piece_rate_cents: 8000`), scheduled today, not yet clocked in. Used for the piece-rate-up-front and first clock-in/out scenarios.
- Job `e86bcd8d-2ce3-4070-a212-24446c9be6bb` — second job assigned to qa-cleaner (scheduled 2026-07-15), used as the "next job" for the already-clocked-in-elsewhere and clock-out-then-clock-in scenarios.
- Job `0d5fd401-dd4e-4da6-8d01-82c4c26b3ef7` — assigned to a different cleaner (user id 3), used for the not-my-job redirect test.
- Job `ec8337a9-12f8-4124-afb1-c8a99b229449` — freshly created hourly job (`hourly_rate_cents: 2500`) with an already-open time entry clocked in 2 hours ago (`clocked_in_at: now() - 2h`), used for the hourly-earnings-on-clock-out scenario.

## What To Test

- `/field/jobs/7a048bd4-...` before clocking in: shows `$80.00` and no "/hr" or "per hour" text (piece-rate up front).
- Tap `[data-test='clock-in-button']` → "Clocked in" text and `[data-test='elapsed-time']` appear.
- Open `/field/jobs/e86bcd8d-...` (still clocked in on the first job) and tap Clock In → warned it's still clocked in to the first job's client, must clock out there first; no `[data-test='elapsed-time']` appears on this second job.
- Go back to `/field/jobs/7a048bd4-...` and tap `[data-test='clock-out-button']` → "Clocked out", `[data-test='worked-time']`, and job-earnings still `$80.00` (piece rate, time-independent).
- Now open `/field/jobs/e86bcd8d-...` and tap Clock In → succeeds this time: "Clocked in" + elapsed-time.
- Attempt to open `/field/jobs/0d5fd401-...` (someone else's job) as qa-cleaner → redirected to `/field` with an error flash containing "not assigned"; never renders the job page.
- Open `/field/jobs/ec8337a9-...` (2 hours already clocked, hourly $25/hr) and tap Clock Out → shows `$50.00` job earnings.
- On `/field`, note the pay-period total before/after these clock-outs — it should grow by the resolved amounts ($80 piece-rate + $50 hourly = $130) once both time entries are resolved.
- `/field`'s earnings card shows `[data-test='drive-time-policy']` stating drive time is unpaid (account's `drive_time_policy: :unpaid`).

## Result Path

No result.md — findings via `create_issue`, outcome via `submit_qa_result`.

## Setup Notes

`CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.current_pay_period/1` derives the pay period from the account-wide max `clocked_in_at`, not from `Date.utc_today()` directly — since all seeded and live-driven entries are today (2026-07-08), this stays consistent. `list_job_time_summaries/2` only counts jobs that have at least one time_entry row, even for piece-rate jobs, so every scenario here drives a real clock-in/out rather than relying on job.status alone.

defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTracking do
  @moduledoc """
  Clock-in/out per job, hourly and piece-rate pay, transparent
  per-job and pay-period earnings, and payroll-ready CSV export.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account. Money is
  always integer cents; `CleanerCrm.Money` formats it for display and
  `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings` does the cents math.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.{Earnings, PayRate, PayrollExport, TimeEntry}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.{Scope, User}

  ## Clocking in and out

  @doc """
  Clocks the scope's user in to `job`. Fails closed: `{:error,
  :not_assigned}` if the job isn't theirs, `{:error,
  {:already_clocked_in, other_job}}` if they're still on the clock
  somewhere else.
  """
  def clock_in(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- ensure_assigned(job, scope.user),
         :ok <- ensure_not_already_clocked_in(scope, job) do
      create_time_entry(scope, %{job_id: job.id, clocked_in_at: DateTime.utc_now()})
    end
  end

  @doc "Clocks the scope's user out of their open entry on `job`."
  def clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :not_clocked_in}

      entry ->
        entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: DateTime.utc_now()}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end

  defp ensure_assigned(%Job{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}, %User{id: cleaner_id}), do: :ok
  defp ensure_assigned(_job, _user), do: {:error, :not_assigned}

  defp ensure_not_already_clocked_in(%Scope{user: user} = scope, %Job{id: job_id}) do
    case open_time_entry_for_cleaner(scope, user.id) do
      nil -> :ok
      %TimeEntry{job_id: ^job_id} -> :ok
      %TimeEntry{} = entry -> {:error, {:already_clocked_in, Repo.preload(entry, :job).job}}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a resolved (or open, if `clocked_out_at` is omitted or
  `nil`) time entry directly. The sanctioned bypass
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.time_entry_fixture` seeds through — real
  clock-in/out goes through `clock_in/2` and `clock_out/2` above.
  """
  def create_time_entry(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, fetch!(attrs, :job_id))

    %TimeEntry{account_id: account_id, job_id: job.id, cleaner_id: job.cleaner_id}
    |> TimeEntry.changeset(attrs)

# QA Story 845: Report damage, missing items, or unsafe conditions from the job

Run a full QA session for this story. Two phases: write a testing brief,
then execute it. The playbook below has the detailed procedure.

**App URL:** Run `mix run -e 'IO.puts(CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url())'`.

## Story description

As a cleaner, I want to file a timestamped photo report of damage, missing items, or unsafe conditions directly from the job screen, so that the office and client hear it from the record — not a text thread — and I'm protected from blame. (Research: damage/missing-item reporting is standard in STR tools and absent elsewhere; lone-worker safety is under-served — pain-points §2.7, §3.3)

## Acceptance criteria

- Cleaner files a damage report from the job screen
- Report carries the filing time and cleaner automatically
- Submitted report cannot be altered
- Damage report without a photo is blocked
- Unsafe-condition report can be filed without a photo
- Office is notified when a report is filed

A photo is required for damage/missing-item reports (enforced by `CleanerCrm.Quality.file_incident_report/3`'s own changeset, not duplicated here); unsafe-condition reports need none. Once filed, a report is immutable — this component never offers an edit or delete affordance. ## Assigns | Assign | Type | Required | Description | |---------------|-------------|----------|------------------------------| | id | string | yes | LiveComponent DOM id | | current_scope | `Scope.t()` | yes | caller scope | | job | `Job.t()` | yes | the job being reported on | ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Quality` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_component alias CleanerCrm.Quality alias CleanerCrm.Repo @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H"""

Report an Issue

Photo (required for damage or a missing item) <.live_file_input upload={@uploads.photo} />
<.form for={@form} id={"#{@id}-form"} data-test="incident-report-form" phx-target={@myself} phx-submit="save" > <.input field={@form[:type]} type="select" label="Type" prompt="Select a type" options={[ {"Damage", "damage"}, {"Missing item", "missing_item"}, {"Unsafe condition", "unsafe_condition"} ]} /> <.input field={@form[:description]} type="textarea" label="Description" />

{msg}

<.button phx-disable-with="Filing...">File Report
  • {report.type}

    {report.description}

    {report.cleaner.email}

    {Calendar.strftime(report.filed_at, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")}

""" end @impl true def mount(socket) do {:ok, allow_upload(socket, :photo, accept: ~w(.jpg .jpeg .png), max_entries: 1)} end @impl true def update(assigns, socket) do {:ok, socket |> assign(assigns) |> assign_new(:form, fn -> blank_form() end) |> assign_new(:incident_reports, fn -> load_incident_reports(assigns.current_scope, assigns.job) end)} end defp blank_form, do: to_form(%{"type" => nil, "description" => nil}, as: :incident) defp load_incident_reports(scope, job) do scope |> Quality.list_incident_reports() |> Enum.filter(&(&1.job_id == job.id)) end @impl true def handle_event("save", %{"incident" => params}, socket) do attrs = maybe_put_photo(params, socket) case Quality.file_incident_report(socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.job, attrs) do {:ok, report} -> report = Repo.preload(report, :cleaner) {:noreply, socket |> assign(:incident_reports, [report | socket.assigns.incident_reports]) |> assign(:form, blank_form())} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :incident))} end end defp maybe_put_photo(params, socket) do case socket.assigns.uploads.photo.entries do [] -> params _entries -> [storage_key] = consume_uploaded_entries(socket, :photo, fn %{path: path}, entry -> {:ok, store_upload!(path, entry)} end) Map.put(params, "photo", %{ "storage_key" => storage_key, "upload_state" => "uploaded", "captured_at" => DateTime.utc_now() }) end end defp store_upload!(path, entry) do dest_dir = Path.join([:code.priv_dir(:cleaner_crm), "static", "uploads"]) File.mkdir_p!(dest_dir) filename = "#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}-#{entry.client_name}" File.cp!(path, Path.join(dest_dir, filename)) "/uploads/#{filename}" end defp photo_errors(%{source: %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset}) do changeset.errors |> Keyword.get_values(:photo) |> Enum.map(fn {msg, _opts} -> "A photo " <> msg <> "." end) end defp photo_errors(_form), do: [] end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story845.Criterion7178Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 845 — Report damage, missing items, or unsafe conditions from the job
  Criterion 7178 — Cleaner files a damage report from the job screen
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a cleaner files a damage report directly from the job screen" do
    scenario "cleaner files a damage report from the job screen" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        owner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{owner_conn: owner_conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "cleaner Ana is logged in on her assigned, in-progress job", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{email: "ana@example.com"})

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            status: :in_progress
          })

        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(build_conn(), cleaner)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, cleaner: cleaner, job: job, conn: conn})}
      end

      when_ "Ana files a damage report with a description and a photo of the damage", context do
        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        photo_upload =
          file_input(job_live, "[data-test='incident-photo-upload']", :photo, [
            %{name: "broken_lamp.jpg", content: "photo-bytes", type: "image/jpeg"}
          ])

        render_upload(photo_upload, "broken_lamp.jpg")

        job_live
        |> form("[data-test='incident-report-form']",
          incident: %{
            type: "damage",
            description: "Living room floor lamp is cracked and will not stand upright"
          }
        )
        |> render_submit()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :job_live, job_live)}
      end

      then_ "the damage report appears on the job screen as filed", context do
        assert has_element?(context.job_live, "[data-test='incident-report-item']")

        assert render(context.job_live) =~
                 "Living room floor lamp is cracked and will not stand upright"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the owner sees the filed damage report when reviewing incidents", context do
        {:ok, _review_live, html} = live(context.owner_conn, ~p"/quality")

        assert html =~ "Living room floor lamp is cracked and will not stand upright"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end
