content.text: This is a genuine, high-impact bug: the photo upload input isn't nested inside the incident report `<form>`, so Phoenix LiveView's upload channel never activates in a real browser, even though the automated test suite passes (its test helpers bypass the DOM). Let me file this.

input.title: Incident report photo upload never activates in a real browser — damage/missing-item reports cannot be filed with a photo
input.description:
Reproduction: on /field/jobs/:id, in the "Report an Issue" panel, select a photo via the file input under [data-test='incident-photo-upload'], then submit [data-test='incident-report-form'] with type=damage and a description. Result: "A photo is required for this report type." every time, even though a real file was selected (confirmed via JS: el.files.length === 1, correct filename).

Root cause: in lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/field_live/incident_form_component.ex, the `<.live_file_input upload={@uploads.photo} />` (around line 39) lives in a plain `<div data-test="incident-photo-upload" phx-target={@myself}>` that is a SIBLING of, not nested inside, the `<.form for={@form} ... phx-submit="save">` (line 42+). Phoenix LiveView's upload JS hook (Phoenix.LiveFileUpload) needs the file input to be inside a form bound with phx-change/phx-submit to establish the upload channel handshake. Confirmed via DOM inspection after selecting a file: the input's `data-phx-active-refs`, `data-phx-preflighted-refs`, and `data-phx-done-refs` all stay empty strings -- the file is selected in the browser (`input.files` is populated) but LiveView never registers it as an upload entry. Manually dispatching `input`/`change` events on the element made no difference. By the time the form's "save" event reaches the server, `socket.assigns.uploads.photo.entries == []`, so `maybe_put_photo/2` never attaches a photo and the changeset correctly (but for the wrong underlying reason) rejects the damage report as photo-less.

Verified via psql: zero rows in `photos` have a non-null `incident_report_id`, confirming no incident report has ever been filed with a photo through the real UI in this environment.

Why the automated BDD suite doesn't catch this: the spex tests (criteria 7178, 7179, 7184) use `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.file_input/4` + `render_upload/2`, which drive the upload channel directly through the test harness's internal API regardless of DOM nesting -- they never exercise the actual browser/JS upload handshake, so this DOM-structure bug is invisible to them.

Impact: cleaners can never successfully attach a photo to a damage or missing-item report through the real app. Since a photo is required for those two types, this makes it impossible to file either report type at all -- only unsafe-condition reports (no photo required) work. This is the story's primary use case (damage reporting) being non-functional.

Fix: move `<.live_file_input upload={@uploads.photo} />` inside the `<.form>` element (or otherwise ensure the file input is a descendant of a form bound with phx-change/phx-submit targeting this component).

# QA Story 846: Keep the same cleaner on the same home

Run a full QA session for this story. Two phases: write a testing brief,
then execute it. The playbook below has the detailed procedure.

**App URL:** Run `mix run -e 'IO.puts(CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url())'`.

## Story description

As a cleaning business owner, I want recurring plans to prefer the client's assigned cleaner and warn me when I assign someone else, so that clients get the consistency they pay for and retention stays high. (Research: same-cleaner-to-same-home matching is a distinct residential pain — pain-points §3.1)

- Owner sets a preferred cleaner on a recurring plan

1 defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.PlanFormComponent do 2 @moduledoc """ 3 Create or edit a recurring plan, with series-wide conflict detection 4 that updates live as the owner fills in the form. 5 6 Saving a plan never blocks on conflicts — every occurrence still 7 gets created and (if a preferred cleaner is set) still assigned to 8 them. Conflicts stay visible after a save so the owner can keep 9 reviewing/overriding them; this component intentionally does not 10 navigate away on its own after saving (see `PlanLive`). 11 12 ## Assigns 13 14 | Assign | Type | Required | Description | 15 |---------------|---------------------|----------|-------------------------------------------------| 16 | id | string | yes | LiveComponent DOM id | 17 | current_scope | `Scope.t()` | yes | caller scope, used for all context calls | 18 | action | `:new \\| :edit` | yes | which mode the form is in | 19 | plan | `RecurringPlan.t()` | yes | blank `%RecurringPlan{}` for `:new`, loaded for `:edit` | 20 21 On successful save, sends `{__MODULE__, {:saved, plan}}` to the 22 parent. 23 24 ## Dependencies 25 26 - `CleanerCrm.Scheduling` 27 """ 28 29 use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_component 30 31 import Ecto.Query, warn: false 32 33 alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Property 34 alias CleanerCrm.Repo 35 alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling 36 37 @impl true 38 def render(assigns) do 39 ~H""" 40
41 <.header>{form_title(@action)} 42 43 <.form 44 for={@form} 45 id={"#{@id}-form"} 46 data-test="plan-form" 47 phx-target={@myself} 48 phx-change="validate" 49 phx-submit="save" 50 > 51 <.input 52 field={@form[:property_id]} 53 type="select" 54 label="Property" 55 prompt="Select a property" 56 options={property_options(@properties)} 57 /> 58 <.input 59 field={@form[:cleaner_id]} 60 type="select" 61 label="Preferred Cleaner" 62 prompt="No preferred cleaner" 63 options={cleaner_options(@cleaners)} 64 /> 65 <.input 66 field={@form[:recurrence]} 67 type="select" 68 label="Recurrence" 69 prompt="Select a cadence" 70 options={[{"Weekly", "weekly"}, {"Biweekly", "biweekly"}, {"Every 4 weeks", "monthly"}]} 71 /> 72 <.input field={@form[:start_date]} type="date" label="Start Date" /> 73 <.input field={@form[:occurrence_count]} type="number" label="Number of Visits" min="1" /> 74 75
80 81 Visit {conflict.index} ({conflict.date}) has a scheduling conflict: {conflict_reason_text( 82 conflict.reason 83 )}. 84 85 <.button 86 type="button" 87 data-test={"override-conflict-#{conflict.index}"} 88 phx-target={@myself} 89 phx-click="override_conflict" 90 phx-value-index={conflict.index} 91 > 92 Override 93 94
95 96
97 <.button 98 type="button" 99 data-test="save-plan-button" 100 phx-target={@myself} 101 phx-click="save" 102 phx-disable-with="Saving..." 103 > 104 Save Plan 105 106
107 108
109 """ 110 end 111 112 @impl true 113 def update(%{plan: plan} = assigns, socket) do 114 changeset = Scheduling.change_recurring_plan(assigns.current_scope, plan, %{}) 115 116 {:ok, 117 socket 118 |> assign(assigns) 119 |> assign(:overridden, MapSet.new()) 120 |> assign(:properties, list_properties(assigns.current_scope)) 121 |> assign(:cleaners, Scheduling.list_cleaners(assigns.current_scope)) 122 |> assign_form_and_conflicts(changeset)} 123 end 124 125 @impl true 126 def handle_event("validate", %{"plan" => params}, socket) do 127 changeset = 128 socket.assigns.current_scope 129 |> Scheduling.change_recurring_plan(socket.assigns.plan, params) 130 |> Map.put(:action, :validate) 131 132 {:noreply, assign_form_and_conflicts(socket, changeset)} 133 end 134 135 def handle_event("override_conflict", %{"index" => index}, socket) do 136 index = String.to_integer(index) 137 138 {:noreply, 139 socket 140 |> Phoenix.Component.update(:overridden, &MapSet.put(&1, index)) 141 |> Phoenix.Component.update( 142 :conflicts, 143 &Enum.reject(&1, fn conflict -> conflict.index == index end) 144 )} 145 end 146 147 # The save button is a plain `phx-click`, not a form submit — the 148 # board's own conflict-review flow drives it that way (see the 149 # spex). It carries no params of its own, so it saves whatever the 150 # last "validate" pass put in the form. 151 def handle_event("save", %{"plan" => params}, socket), do: save_plan(socket, params) 152 153 def handle_event("save", _params, socket), 154 do: save_plan(socket, socket.assigns.form.params || %{}) 155 156 defp save_plan(socket, params) do 157 case Scheduling.create_recurring_plan(socket.assigns.current_scope, params) do 158 {:ok, {plan, _jobs}} -> 159 notify_parent({:saved, plan}) 160 changeset = Scheduling.change_recurring_plan(socket.assigns.current_scope, plan, %{}) 161 162 {:noreply, 163 socket 164 |> assign(:plan, plan) 165 |> assign_form_and_conflicts(changeset)} 166 167 {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> 168 {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :plan))} 169 end 170 end 171 172 defp assign_form_and_conflicts(socket, changeset) do 173 draft = Ecto.Changeset.apply_changes(changeset) 174 175 conflicts = 176 socket.assigns.current_scope 177 |> Scheduling.preview_conflicts(draft) 178 |> Enum.reject(&MapSet.member?(socket.assigns.overridden, &1.index)) 179 180 socket 181 |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset, as: :plan)) 182 |> assign(:conflicts, conflicts) 183 end 184 185 defp notify_parent(msg), do: send(self(), {__MODULE__, msg}) 186 187 defp list_properties(%{active_account_id: account_id}) do 188 Property 189 |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id) 190 |> order_by([p], asc: p.service_address) 191 |> Repo.all() 192 end 193 194 defp property_options(properties), do: Enum.map(properties, &{&1.service_address, &1.id}) 195 defp cleaner_options(cleaners), do: Enum.map(cleaners, &{&1.name || &1.email, &1.id}) 196 197 defp conflict_reason_text(:unavailable), do: "the cleaner is unavailable that day" 198 defp conflict_reason_text(:overlap), do: "it overlaps another booking" 199 200 defp form_title(:new), do: "New Recurring Plan" 201 defp form_title(:edit), do: "Edit Recurring Plan" 202 end 203

It carries no params of its own, so it saves whatever the # last "validate" pass put in the form. def handle_event("save", %{"plan" => params}, socket), do: save_plan(socket, params) def handle_event("save", _params, socket), do: save_plan(socket, socket.assigns.form.params || %{}) defp save_plan(socket, params) do case Scheduling.create_recurring_plan(socket.assigns.current_scope, params) do {:ok, {plan, _jobs}} -> notify_parent({:saved, plan}) changeset = Scheduling.change_recurring_plan(socket.assigns.current_scope, plan, %{}) {:noreply, socket |> assign(:plan, plan) |> assign_form_and_conflicts(changeset)} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :plan))} end end defp assign_form_and_conflicts(socket, changeset) do draft = Ecto.Changeset.apply_changes(changeset) conflicts = socket.assigns.current_scope |> Scheduling.preview_conflicts(draft) |> Enum.reject(&MapSet.member?(socket.assigns.overridden, &1.index)) socket |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset, as: :plan)) |> assign(:conflicts, conflicts) end defp notify_parent(msg), do: send(self(), {__MODULE__, msg}) defp list_properties(%{active_account_id: account_id}) do Property |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id) |> order_by([p], asc: p.service_address) |> Repo.all() end defp property_options(properties), do: Enum.map(properties, &{&1.service_address, &1.id}) defp cleaner_options(cleaners), do: Enum.map(cleaners, &{&1.name || &1.email, &1.id}) defp conflict_reason_text(:unavailable), do: "the cleaner is unavailable that day" defp conflict_reason_text(:overlap), do: "it overlaps another booking" defp form_title(:new), do: "New Recurring Plan" defp form_title(:edit), do: "Edit Recurring Plan" end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story846.Criterion7196Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 846 — Keep the same cleaner on the same home

  when creating a recurring plan for a property, the owner designates a
  preferred cleaner, and the plan's own generated visit is assigned to
  that cleaner.

  Assumes `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.PlanFormComponent` (opened from
  `/schedule/plans/new`, per story 833's own specs) exposes a
  `[data-test='plan-form']` whose `cleaner_id` field designates the
  plan's preferred cleaner — `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan`
  "records the client's preferred cleaner" per its architecture spec —
  and a `[data-test='save-plan-button']` that saves the plan and
  materializes its occurrence(s) immediately, per criterion 7143.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens

  spex "the owner designates a preferred cleaner when creating a recurring plan" do
    scenario "owner sets a preferred cleaner on a recurring plan" do
      given_(:logged_in_owner_with_account)

      given_ "a client \"Jamie Rivera\" with a property exists", context do
        client_path = create_client(context.conn, "Jamie Rivera")

        property_path =
          create_property(context.conn, client_path, %{service_address: "12 Oak Lane"})

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           client_path: client_path,
           property_id: id_from_path(property_path)
         })}
      end

      given_ "a cleaner \"Alex Morgan\" is available for assignment", context do
        cleaner_path = create_cleaner(context.conn, "Alex Morgan")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :cleaner_id, id_from_path(cleaner_path))}
      end

      when_ "the owner creates a recurring plan and sets Alex Morgan as the preferred cleaner",
            context do
        {:ok, plan_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule/plans/new")

        plan_live
        |> form("[data-test='plan-form']",
          plan: %{
            property_id: context.property_id,
            cleaner_id: context.cleaner_id,
            recurrence: "weekly",
            start_date: Date.to_iso8601(first_visit_date()),
            occurrence_count: 1
          }
        )
        |> render_change()

        plan_live
        |> element("[data-test='save-plan-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the plan's generated visit is assigned to the preferred cleaner, Alex Morgan",
            context do
        {:ok, board_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        [job_id] = job_ids(html)

        assert has_element?(
                 board_live,
                 "[data-test='cleaner-column-#{context.cleaner_id}'] [data-test='job-#{job_id}']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp first_visit_date, do: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)
  defp id_from_path(path), do: path |> String.split("/") |> List.last()

    ~r/data-test="job-([0-9a-f-]+)"/
    |> Regex.scan(html)
    |> Enum.map(fn [_, id] -> id end)
    |> Enum.uniq()
  end

  defp create_client(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='client-form']", client: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_property(conn, client_path, attrs) do
    "/clients/" <> client_id = client_path

    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/#{client_id}/properties/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: attrs)
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='cleaner-form']", cleaner: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end
end

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: attrs)
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_cleaner(conn, name) do

# QA Story 843: Get loud, acknowledged alerts when my schedule changes

Run a full QA session for this story. Two phases: write a testing brief,
then execute it. The playbook below has the detailed procedure.

**App URL:** Run `mix run -e 'IO.puts(CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url())'`.

## Story description

As a cleaner, I want schedule changes (added/moved/cancelled jobs) pushed to me as notifications that I explicitly acknowledge — with the office seeing unacknowledged changes — so that mid-day changes actually reach me and same-day cleanings aren't silently missed. (Research: undelivered assignment changes are the most common cause of missed same-day cleanings — pain-points §2.4)

## Acceptance criteria

- Moved job notifies the cleaner
- Cancelled job notifies the cleaner
- Acknowledging clears the pending change
- Unacknowledged change keeps prompting
- Office sees who has not acknowledged
- Never-acknowledged same-day change escalates
- Push failure falls back to SMS

## Cancelled job's schedule-change notification is invisible to the office and can never escalate (ID: 7df52070-dc5a-49fc-b3ac-925cecce6f3d)

**Severity:** high | **Scope:** app | **Status:** resolved | **Story:** 843

Reproduction: as owner on /schedule, cancel a cleaner's job via [data-test='job-<id>-cancel-button']. A schedule_change notification (kind=schedule_change, status=pending, channel=push, summary="Cancelled") is correctly created and the cleaner sees the "Cancelled" alert on /field (confirmed via psql + browser).

However, `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.list_jobs/1` (lib/cleaner_crm/scheduling.ex:143) filters `where j.status != :cancelled`, so a cancelled job's row (and its `[data-test='job-<id>-ack-status']` / `[data-test='job-<id>-notification-channel']` indicators) disappears from ScheduleLive.Index entirely the moment it's cancelled.

Two consequences, both against story 843's acceptance criteria:
1. "Office sees who has not acknowledged" fails specifically for cancellations: there is no way for the office to see whether the cleaner has acknowledged a job cancellation, since the board never renders that job's row again.
2. "Never-acknowledged same-day change escalates" never fires for cancellations: `CleanerCrm.Notifications.maybe_escalate/1` (lib/cleaner_crm/notifications.ex) — the function that flips a stale pending notification to :escalated and re-sends via SMS — is only invoked from `latest_schedule_change_for_job/2`, which is only ever called by ScheduleLive.Index.schedule_change_alert/2 for jobs in `@jobs`. Since cancelled jobs are excluded from that list, a cancellation notification can sit `pending` forever with no escalation check ever running, no matter how long it goes unacknowledged.

This is arguably the highest-stakes case for the whole story: a cleaner who never sees/acknowledges that their job was cancelled might show up anyway, and the office has no way to notice the unacknowledged cancellation because the row is gone.

Expected: the office should still be able to see acknowledgment status (and escalation) for a cancelled job's schedule-change notification, e.g. by not filtering cancelled jobs out of the board (or showing them in a distinct "cancelled" section) at least while they carry an unacknowledged/escalated notification.

Verified via: browser session as qa-owner/qa-cleaner, job dbd5a7b7-5390-423f-9fab-ca100cdcced8, and psql confirming the notification row (id 5dd646b7-e1d6-450b-9734-a2395e66cd2a) stays status=pending indefinitely with no escalation path reachable.

**Resolution:** Cancelled jobs with an unacknowledged schedule_change notification now stay on the board. Added Notifications.job_ids_with_unacknowledged_schedule_change/1 (latest-per-job status != :acknowledged); Scheduling.list_jobs/2 gained an :include_cancelled_ids opt (default [] — unchanged behavior for other callers); ScheduleLive.Index.load_week/1 passes that id set through and job_card now shows a muted "Cancelled" badge while keeping ack-status/channel selectors, so office visibility and read-time escalation work for cancellations too.

## Incident report photo upload never activates in a real browser — damage/missing-item reports cannot be filed with a photo (ID: ed815749-b973-40e9-b220-a58ed767c4e1)

**Severity:** high | **Scope:** app | **Status:** resolved | **Story:** 845

Reproduction: on /field/jobs/:id, in the "Report an Issue" panel, select a photo via the file input under [data-test='incident-photo-upload'], then submit [data-test='incident-report-form'] with type=damage and a description. Result: "A photo is required for this report type." every time, even though a real file was selected (confirmed via JS: el.files.length === 1, correct filename).

Root cause: in lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/field_live/incident_form_component.ex, the `<.live_file_input upload={@uploads.photo} />` (around line 39) lives in a plain `<div data-test="incident-photo-upload" phx-target={@myself}>` that is a SIBLING of, not nested inside, the `<.form for={@form} ... phx-submit="save">` (line 42+). Phoenix LiveView's upload JS hook (Phoenix.LiveFileUpload) needs the file input to be inside a form bound with phx-change/phx-submit to establish the upload channel handshake. Confirmed via DOM inspection after selecting a file: the input's `data-phx-active-refs`, `data-phx-preflighted-refs`, and `data-phx-done-refs` all stay empty strings -- the file is selected in the browser (`input.files` is populated) but LiveView never registers it as an upload entry. Manually dispatching `input`/`change` events on the element made no difference. By the time the form's "save" event reaches the server, `socket.assigns.uploads.photo.entries == []`, so `maybe_put_photo/2` never attaches a photo and the changeset correctly (but for the wrong underlying reason) rejects the damage report as photo-less.

Verified via psql: zero rows in `photos` have a non-null `incident_report_id`, confirming no incident report has ever been filed with a photo through the real UI in this environment.

Why the automated BDD suite doesn't catch this: the spex tests (criteria 7178, 7179, 7184) use `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.file_input/4` + `render_upload/2`, which drive the upload channel directly through the test harness's internal API regardless of DOM nesting -- they never exercise the actual browser/JS upload handshake, so this DOM-structure bug is invisible to them.

Impact: cleaners can never successfully attach a photo to a damage or missing-item report through the real app. Since a photo is required for those two types, this makes it impossible to file either report type at all -- only unsafe-condition reports (no photo required) work. This is the story's primary use case (damage reporting) being non-functional.

Fix: move `<.live_file_input upload={@uploads.photo} />` inside the `<.form>` element (or otherwise ensure the file input is a descendant of a form bound with phx-change/phx-submit targeting this component).

**Resolution:** Moved the live_file_input (with its data-test wrapper and phx-target) inside the incident-report <.form> in IncidentFormComponent so the upload channel binds to a real <form> element (LiveView's client JS requires inputEl.form to be non-null to push file progress/input events). Added phx-change="validate" on the form and a handle_event("validate", ...) clause to keep the standard LiveView upload validate/save flow. All existing data-test attributes and event names (save, incident-report-form, incident-photo-upload) preserved.

Verified: MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors clean; mix spex 845_*/ 6/6 green; mix spex 842_*/ 7/7 green; mix spex 839_*/ 7/7 green; mix test 160/160 green; mix format clean (no diff).

Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Same issue id: 7df52070-dc5a-49fc-b3ac-925cecce6f3d.
